docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Error Response (400 Bad Request - No search parameters):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "no_search_parameters_provided"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Invalid integer parameter):

The level, min_level, max_level, and meeting_point parameters must be valid integers. If a non-numeric value is provided, the API returns:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "invalid_level"
}
Parameter Error message level invalid_level min_level invalid_min_level max_level invalid_max_level meeting_point invalid_meeting_point_id

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Invalid area format):

The area parameter must be a string area code (e.g., DXB, AUH). Numeric values are rejected:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "invalid_area_format"
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) on trip titles
  • Query must be at least 3 characters long
  • Results are ordered by start_time (descending), then by id (ascending)
  • Results are paginated using standard pagination (20 items per page by default)
  • Level filtering: Use level for exact level match, or min_level/max_level for range filtering
  • Example: ?level=10 returns only Newbie trips
  • Example: ?min_level=100 returns Intermediate and higher level trips
  • Example: ?max_level=100 returns Newbie and Intermediate level trips
  • Date filtering: Use start_date_min/max and end_date_min/max to filter by date ranges
  • Trips that have ended (cut_off is in the past) are automatically excluded from results
  • If end_date_max is set without end_date_min, only trips ending on or before that date are included
  • Similarly for start dates
  • Meeting point filtering: Use meeting_point to filter by exact meeting point ID
  • Area filtering: Use area to filter by meeting point area code (e.g., DXB, AUH, AAN, NOR, LIW)
  • No approval status filter: This endpoint does NOT support filtering by approvalStatus. It searches all trips regardless of approval status. Use the main trip list (GET /api/trips/) for approval status filtering.
  • Permission Required: Users must have SEARCH_TRIPS permission. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above.
  • Performance Note: This endpoint searches trip titles efficiently. Searching by trip lead's user info (username, first name, last name) requires additional database joins and can be slower with many trips. Use title-based search for better performance.
  • User-specific information: For authenticated users, the response includes trip-specific registration status:
  • isRegistered: Whether the authenticated user is registered for this trip
  • isWaitlisted: Whether the authenticated user is on the waitlist for this trip
  • waitlistCount: Current number of users on the waitlist
  • registeredCount: Current number of users registered for this trip

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Finding specific trips by title search
  • Browsing available trips for a specific level (e.g., Newbie trips only)
  • Discovering trip activities by date range
  • Finding trips at specific meeting points
  • Exploring trips in specific geographic areas
  • Checking trip history for a user or level
  • Building trip calendars or schedules

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing trips, including creating, viewing, registering, and managing participants.

docs.title: Trip Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Creation: A trip is created via a POST request. Depending on the creator's permissions, it may be automatically approved or require manual approval.
  2. Approval: Trips requiring approval must be approved by a user with the appropriate permissions before they become visible to regular members.
  3. Registration: Once a trip is approved, members can register for it until the cut_off time is reached or the capacity is filled.
  4. Waitlist: If a trip is full and allow_waitlist is enabled, members can join the waitlist. They can optionally specify a vehicle when joining. The vehicle is stored and used when moved to registered. Members will be automatically moved to the registered list if a spot becomes available.
  5. Check-in/Check-out: The trip lead or a deputy can check members in and out of the trip.

docs.title: List and Retrieve Trips
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/

    • Retrieves a list of all approved trips.

    • Query Parameters:

      Parameter Type Description lead integer Filter by trip lead (member ID) deputy_leads integer Filter by deputy lead (member ID) meeting_point integer Filter by meeting point ID meeting_point__area string Filter by meeting point area code (e.g., DXB, AUH) level__id integer Filter by level ID level__numeric_level integer Filter by exact numeric level level__numeric_level__range string Filter by numeric level range (e.g., 100,500) approval_status string Filter by approval status (A=Approved, P=Pending, C=Cancelled) start_time_after datetime Filter trips starting after this date start_time_before datetime Filter trips starting before this date end_time_after datetime Filter trips ending after this date end_time_before datetime Filter trips ending before this date registered boolean Filter to only trips where the authenticated user is registered (true) or not registered (false). Requires authentication. waitlisted boolean Filter to only trips where the authenticated user is on the waitlist (true) or not waitlisted (false). Requires authentication. page integer Page number (default: 1) page_size integer Number of results per page (default: 20)

    Note: Both camelCase and snake_case parameter names are accepted (e.g., approvalStatus and approval_status are equivalent, startTimeAfter and start_time_after are equivalent).

  • GET /api/trips/{id}/

    • Retrieves the full details of a single trip, including registered members and the waitlist.
    • Contact Info: The trip lead and deputy leads' contact info (email, phone) is always visible to authenticated users. Other members' contact info requires VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission.

docs.title: Create a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips

    Note: The create endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash. This differs from the list/retrieve endpoints which are router-registered.

    • Creates a new trip. The approval_status will be set based on the user's permissions.
    • Request Body: See the CreateTripSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • lead (Member ID)
      • level (Level ID)
      • title
      • start_time
      • end_time
      • cut_off
      • capacity
      • meeting_point (MeetingPoint ID)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., start_time), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., startTime).

docs.title: Update a Trip
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/trips/{id}

    Note: The update/delete endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Updates an existing trip.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when editing is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning editing is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.
    • Request Body: See the UpdateTripSerializer for a list of editable fields.

docs.title: Delete a Trip
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/trips/{id}
    • Deletes a trip. This is a soft-delete, meaning the trip's approval_status is set to CANCELED.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when deleting is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning deleting is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.

docs.title: Approve a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/approve

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Approves a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.
    • The approver is automatically registered as a deputy lead.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>} (optional - defaults to approver's primary vehicle)

docs.title: Decline a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/decline

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Declines a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.
    • Sets the trip's approval_status to REJECTED.
    • Triggers a trip approval notification.
    • Request Body: None required.
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_rejected"}

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
Note: All registration endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

  • POST /api/trips/{id}/register
    • Registers the authenticated user for the trip.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>}
    • Required for regular users: Users must have at least one vehicle registered. Staff users (with EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission) can omit - defaults to their primary vehicle.
    • Returns vehicle_required error if no vehicle is provided.
    • Returns vehicle_not_found error if the vehicle doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the user.
    • Additional validations: trip_not_approved, level_insufficient, trip_cutoff_exceeded, trip_already_registered, trip_full.
    • Success Response: Returns the updated trip object alongside the success message: json {"success": true, "message": "trip_registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }} The trip field contains the complete trip object (same schema as GET /api/trips/{id}/ list response) with updated registeredCount, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, etc. This eliminates the need for a follow-up GET request.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist
    • Adds the authenticated user to the waitlist if the trip is full.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>} (optional - defaults to user's primary vehicle)
    • Returns trip_waitlist_disabled_for_this_trip if waitlist is not enabled.
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_waitlisted", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister
    • Cancels the authenticated user's registration for the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist).
    • Trip leads cannot unregister themselves (trip_lead_cannot_unregister).
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_registration_cancelled", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

docs.title: Force Registration
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/forceregister

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Force-registers a member for a trip, bypassing level requirements and capacity checks. Requires BYPASS_LEVEL_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: json { "member": 123, "vehicle_id": 45 }
    • vehicle_id is optional; defaults to the member's primary vehicle.

docs.title: Participant Management
docs.text:
Note: All participant management endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

  • POST /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist
    • Manually moves a member from the waitlist to the registered list. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>}
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "member_moved_from_waitlist_to_registered"}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/removemember
    • Removes a member from the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist). Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>, "reason": "..."}
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "user_removed_from_trip_registered"} or "user_removed_from_trip_waitlist"
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkin
    • Checks in one or more members to the trip. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkout
    • Checks out one or more members from the trip. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}

Important: The checkin/checkout endpoints use a different response format from other trip endpoints:

json { "succeeded": [1, 2, 3], "failed": [ {"member": 4, "error": "Member is not registered for this trip"} ] }

This is NOT wrapped in the standard {"success": ..., "message": ...} format.

docs.title: Trip Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/comments

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves comments for a specific trip, ordered by most recent first.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Supports ordering via ordering query parameter (field: created).

    Response item fields: comment, member (object with id, username, displayName), trip, created

  • GET/POST/DELETE /api/tripcomments/

    This is the router-registered ViewSet for trip comments (uses trailing slash).

    • GET /api/tripcomments/ - List all comments. Filter by trip or member query params.
    • POST /api/tripcomments/ - Create a comment. Body: {"comment": "...", "trip": <trip_id>}. The member field is automatically set to the authenticated user.
    • DELETE /api/tripcomments/{id}/ - Delete a comment. Requires ownership or DELETE_TRIP_COMMENTS permission.

docs.title: Trip Reports (per trip)
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/tripreports

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves trip reports for a specific trip, ordered by ID.
    • Authentication: Required.

    See Trip Reports for the full CRUD Trip Reports API.

docs.title: Export Registrants
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/exportregistrants

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Exports the trip's registered members as a CSV file.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: CSV file with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="trip_{id}_registrants.csv"
    • CSV Columns: username, name, level, one column per active level for trip counts (e.g., trips_newbie, trips_intermediate), car_brand_model_color, phone, city

docs.title: View Logbooks
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Returns a list of checked-in members for the trip along with their logbook entry (if one exists).
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Each item in the response contains a member object and a logbook_entry object (or null).

    See Digital Logbook for the full logbook API.

docs.title: Member-Specific Trip Endpoints
docs.text:
These endpoints provide trip information tailored to a specific member.

Note: All member-specific endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

docs.title: Member Trip Counts
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/tripcounts
    • Retrieves a summary of a member's completed trips, grouped by trip level.
    • Includes trips where the member was:
      • Registered and checked in (as participant)
      • Lead of the trip
      • Deputy lead of the trip
    • Only includes trips with an APPROVED status.
    • Trips are counted once even if member has multiple roles (lead + registered).

docs.title: Member Trip History
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory
    • Retrieves a paginated history of a member's trips.
    • Query Parameters: checked_in (boolean, filter for checked-in trips only), start_time (datetime filter).
    • Permissions: Own history always viewable. Viewing another member's history requires VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission or superuser.

    • Note: This endpoint only includes trips with an APPROVED status.

See also the Digital Logbook page for information on how to manage logbook entries for a trip.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing level upgrade requests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Members can request to be upgraded to a higher level. This process involves creating a request, which is then reviewed and voted on by authorized members (e.g., Marshals, Board Members).

docs.title: List and Retrieve Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/
    • Retrieves a list of upgrade requests. Requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single upgrade request.

docs.title: Get Member Upgrade Eligibility
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a detailed report on a member's eligibility for an upgrade to the next potential level. This report includes a breakdown of met/unmet requirements based on minimum trips at the current level and required logbook skills for the next level.
    • Authorization:
      • A member can view their own eligibility (when {id} matches request.user.id).
      • Members with the VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission can view the eligibility of any member.
      • Superusers can view any member's eligibility.

    • Response Structure (Example):

      Note: The backend builds the response in snake_case, but the camelCase middleware automatically converts the keys. The response you receive will use camelCase.

      json { "memberId": 1, "memberUsername": "testuser", "currentLevel": { "id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10 }, "nextPotentialLevel": { "id": 2, "name": "Intermediate", "numericLevel": 100 }, "upgradeRequirements": [ { "type": "min_trips", "name": "Minimum trips for current level", "requiredValue": 5, "currentValue": 3, "met": false, "description": "You need 5 trips at your current level (completed at this level).", "recentTripsAtLevel": [ { "tripId": 10, "title": "Desert Crossing", "startTime": "2026-01-15T09:00:00+04:00", "lead": {"id": 1, "username": "leader1"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10} }, { "tripId": 9, "title": "Mountain Trail", "startTime": "2025-12-20T08:00:00+04:00", "lead": {"id": 2, "username": "leader2"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10} } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skillId": 101, "skillName": "Basic Recovery", "requiredCount": 2, "currentCount": 1, "met": false, "description": "Complete 'Basic Recovery' 2 times.", "signatures": [ { "tripId": 15, "signedBy": {"id": 5, "username": "verifier_user"}, "signedDate": "2026-02-01T10:30:00+04:00" } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skillId": 102, "skillName": "Tyre Changing", "requiredCount": 1, "currentCount": 1, "met": true, "description": "Complete 'Tyre Changing' 1 time.", "signatures": [ { "tripId": 12, "signedBy": {"id": 6, "username": "another_verifier"}, "signedDate": "2026-01-25T14:00:00+04:00" } ] } ], "isEligibleForUpgrade": false }

docs.title: Create an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/

    • Creates a new upgrade request.
    • Eligibility Check: Before creation, the system checks if the applicant is eligible for an upgrade based on minimum trips at their current level and required logbook skills for the target level. If the applicant is not eligible, or is already at the highest available level, the request will be rejected with a 400 Bad Request status and a detailed error message listing unmet requirements.
    • Request Body: See the CreateUpgradeRequestSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • applicant (Member ID of the person being nominated for upgrade)
      • target_level (Level ID)
      • applicant_reason (Text description)
      • nominated_voters (List of Member IDs)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., target_level), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., targetLevel).

docs.title: Update an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Updates an existing upgrade request. Requires EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Voting and Approval
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/vote

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Casts a vote on an upgrade request. Requires VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"vote": "Y"} (or "N" for No, "D" for Defer)
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "vote_accepted"}
    • Error: Returns upgrade_request_not_open_for_votes if the request status is not NEW or IN_PROGRESS. Returns invalid_vote_choice:<value> for unrecognized vote values.
    • Note: The first vote on a NEW request automatically moves its status to IN_PROGRESS.
    • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/approve/
    • Approves an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/decline/
    • Declines an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"verdict_reason": "..."}

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/comments/
    • Retrieves all comments for a specific upgrade request.
  • POST /api/upgraderequestcomments/
    • Adds a new comment to an upgrade request. Requires CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"upgrade_request": <request_id>, "text": "..."}
  • DELETE /api/upgraderequestcomments/{id}/
    • Deletes a comment. Requires DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Recently Approved Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/latestapproved

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a paginated list of recently approved upgrade requests, ordered by verdict date (most recent first).
    • Authentication: Not required (public endpoint).
    • Pagination: Standard pagination (default 20, max 500).

docs.title: Voted Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/voted

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Returns an array of upgrade request IDs that the current user has voted on. Only includes requests with status NEW or IN_PROGRESS.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: A plain array of integers, e.g., [1, 5, 12, 23]

  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/voted

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Checks whether the current user has voted on a specific upgrade request.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: json { "success": true, "message": { "voted": true } }

docs.title: Vehicles
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing member vehicles. Members can now register multiple vehicles, with a configurable limit set in global settings.

docs.title: Vehicle List
docs.text:
Retrieve all vehicles for the authenticated user.

GET /api/vehicles/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters: - page - Page number (default: 1) - page_size - Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Success Response:

{
  "count": 2,
  "next": null,
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "My Land Cruiser",
      "brand": "TO",
      "brandDisplay": "Toyota",
      "model": "Land Cruiser",
      "year": 2020,
      "color": "White",
      "isPrimary": true
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "name": "Nissan Patrol",
      "brand": "NI",
      "brandDisplay": "Nissan",
      "model": "Patrol",
      "year": 2019,
      "color": "Black",
      "isPrimary": false
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Create Vehicle
docs.text:
Create a new vehicle for the authenticated user.

POST /api/vehicles/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Request Body:

{
  "name": "My Land Cruiser",
  "brand": "TO",
  "model": "Land Cruiser",
  "year": 2020,
  "color": "White",
  "isPrimary": true
}

Fields: | Field | Type | Required | Description | |-------|------|----------|-------------| | name | string | No | User-friendly name for the vehicle | | brand | string | Yes | 2-letter car brand code (e.g., "TO" for Toyota, "NI" for Nissan). See Car Brand Choices for all valid codes. | | model | string | No | Vehicle model | | year | integer | No | Year of manufacture | | color | string | No | Vehicle color | | image | file | No | Vehicle image (multipart/form-data) | | isPrimary | boolean | No | Set as primary vehicle (default: false) |

Validation: - Maximum number of vehicles is limited by vehicle_limit_per_member setting (default: 3) - brand must be a valid CarBrand choice

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": {
    "id": 1,
    "member": 123,
    "name": "My Land Cruiser",
    "brand": "TO",
    "brandDisplay": "Toyota",
    "model": "Land Cruiser",
    "year": 2020,
    "color": "White",
    "image": null,
    "isPrimary": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-03-05T00:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-03-05T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}

Error Response (limit reached):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Maximum number of vehicles (3) reached. Please delete an existing vehicle first."
}

docs.title: Get Vehicle
docs.text:
Get details of a specific vehicle.

GET /api/vehicles/{id}/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": {
    "id": 1,
    "member": 123,
    "name": "My Land Cruiser",
    "brand": "TO",
    "brandDisplay": "Toyota",
    "model": "Land Cruiser",
    "year": 2020,
    "color": "White",
    "image": "/media/vehicles/2026/03/vehicle_abc123.jpg",
    "isPrimary": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-03-05T00:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-03-05T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}

docs.title: Update Vehicle
docs.text:
Update a vehicle's details.

PATCH /api/vehicles/{id}/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Request Body:

{
  "year": 2021,
  "color": "Silver"
}

Note: Users can only update their own vehicles.

docs.title: Delete Vehicle
docs.text:
Delete a vehicle.

DELETE /api/vehicles/{id}/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Note: If the deleted vehicle was the primary vehicle, the most recently created remaining vehicle will be automatically set as primary.

docs.title: Set Primary Vehicle
docs.text:
Set a vehicle as the primary vehicle. Only one vehicle can be primary at a time.

POST /api/vehicles/{id}/set_primary/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,

docs.title: Backend Change Requests — AD4x4 Website
docs.text:
Purpose: Running list of backend API changes needed to support the website portal. Accumulated across development sessions for the backend team to address in one coordinated effort.

For: Django backend team (ap.ad4x4.com)

Last updated: 2026-03-30 (Session #13)

docs.title: #1 — Add server-side filtering for user's registered/waitlisted trips
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/trips/ Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The My Trips portal page needs to show only trips where the logged-in user is registered or waitlisted. The API currently has no server-side filter for this. The frontend is forced to:

  1. Fetch ALL club trips (pageSize=100) — returns trips for every member, not just the requesting user
  2. Filter client-side using the isRegistered / isWaitlisted booleans on each trip object

This causes:

  • ~17-30 second load times on mobile (95 KB payload, 3,305 total trips in the database, only ~17 belong to the user out of the 100 returned)
  • Incomplete data — the Past tab can only show the user's trips that happen to fall within the most recent 100 trips. Older registered trips are invisible.
  • Wasted bandwidth — 80-95% of the downloaded data is discarded

docs.title: Evidence (tested 2026-03-30 with user Elle, ID 21144)
docs.text:
What we fetch Time Payload User's trips in response GET /api/trips/?startTimeBefore=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~1.5-17s 87-95 KB 17 out of 100 results GET /api/trips/?startTimeAfter=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~0.5s 7 KB 2 out of 5 results GET /api/members/21144/triphistory?pageSize=100 ~0.5s 4.6 KB 7 out of 7 (all user's)

We confirmed that registered=true and isRegistered=true query params are silently ignored — the count does not change.

docs.title: Recommended backend changes
docs.text:
Option A (preferred): Add query filters to GET /api/trips/

Add support for these query parameters:

GET /api/trips/?registered=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is registered
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is waitlisted

The data already exists — the API already computes isRegistered and isWaitlisted per-trip in the response. This just needs to be wired up as a queryset filter. This would reduce the Past tab response from 3,305 trips to ~17, and from 95 KB to ~15 KB.

Option B (alternative): Enrich GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory

The triphistory endpoint already returns only the user's trips and is fast (0.5s, 4.6 KB). However, it returns a slim object missing several fields the portal needs:

Currently returned: id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead, level, checkedIn

Missing fields needed by the portal: - image (trip cover photo URL) - meetingPoint (name, lat/lon, link, area) - registeredCount / capacity (registration count vs capacity) - isRegistered / isWaitlisted (registration status badges) - allowWaitlist (UI logic for full-trip warnings) - approvalStatus (filter cancelled/rejected trips)

Adding these fields to the triphistory response would make it a drop-in replacement.

docs.title: Why not fetch individual trip details?
docs.text: We tested GET /api/trips/{id}/ for each trip ID from triphistory. Each call takes 3-13 seconds. Seven sequential calls = ~90s. Even in parallel = ~21s. This is worse than the current approach.

docs.title: #2 — Trailing-slash inconsistency across endpoints
docs.text: Priority: Medium Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Some endpoints require a trailing slash, others return 404 when a slash is present. This causes silent failures when the proxy or client guesses wrong.

Endpoint Without slash With slash Correct form /api/trips 403 (authenticated) 200 With slash /api/levels 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/vehicles 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/choices/carbrand 200 404 Without slash /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings 200 404 Without slash /api/members/request-deletion 200 404 Without slash

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Standardise all endpoints to accept both forms. Django's APPEND_SLASH setting should handle this, but some endpoints (particularly under /api/choices/ and /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings) appear to bypass it.

The frontend proxy currently works around this with redirect-following and 403/405 retry logic, but a consistent backend would be cleaner.

More items will be added in future sessions.

docs.title: Backend Response to Flutter App Performance Audit
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-01 In response to: FRONTEND_API_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-03-31) From: Backend Team

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
We reviewed all 12 findings from the Flutter performance audit. We implemented 4 backend changes that directly address your highest-impact findings. The remaining items are frontend-only optimizations or deferred for now.

What changed on the backend: 1. Trip registration responses now include the updated trip object 2. Cache-Control headers added to static/semi-static endpoints 3. Trip list endpoint now supports registered and waitlisted filters 4. Member trip history endpoint returns richer data (8 new fields)

No breaking changes. All changes are additive — existing response fields and behavior are preserved.

docs.title: T1: Trips List + Home Screen = Duplicate Trip Fetches
docs.text:
Status: No backend change needed (as you noted)

This is a frontend caching concern. The backend now returns Cache-Control headers on static endpoints, but the trips endpoint itself remains uncached since it contains user-specific data (isRegistered, isWaitlisted). Your recommendation to share the upcomingTripsProvider cache between screens is the correct approach.

docs.title: T2: Trip Detail Re-fetched on Every Navigation
docs.text:
Status: No backend change (frontend fix recommended)

Removing the ref.invalidate(tripDetailProvider(trip.id)) call before navigation is the correct fix. The autoDispose + staleness check pattern you already use will handle freshness.

docs.title: T3: Trip Actions Trigger Full List Refresh — IMPLEMENTED
docs.text:
Status: Backend change implemented

All registration endpoints now return the updated trip object in the response body:

POST /api/trips/{id}/register    -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist    -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_waitlisted", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister  -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_registration_cancelled", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

The trip field contains the complete trip object (same schema as GET /api/trips/ list response) with up-to-date registeredCount, waitlistCount, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, etc.

What you need to do on the Flutter side: 1. After a successful registration/waitlist/unregister call, read the trip field from the response 2. Update the local trip in your tripsProvider state with this object 3. Remove the _ref.read(tripsProvider.notifier).refresh() call

API docs reference: See docs/trips.md — Registration section for the full response schema.

docs.title: T4: Member Details Screen — 6+ Waterfall API Calls
docs.text:
Status: Not implementing composite endpoint

We evaluated creating a GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ composite endpoint but decided against it for now. The maintenance cost of a composite endpoint that duplicates 9 existing endpoints is not justified at this project's scale.

What you can do instead: - Use Future.wait() (which you already do) to parallelize the 6+ calls - Cache the results with your existing ApiCacheService - Fix the member_details_screen.dart:28 issue where you create a new MainApiRepository() — use ref.read(mainApiRepositoryProvider) instead to share connection pooling and cache

docs.title: L1: getLogbookSkills() Called by 19 Files — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED
docs.text:
Status: Backend Cache-Control header added

GET /api/logbookskills/ now returns Cache-Control: public, max-age=600 (10 minutes). HTTP clients that respect cache headers will skip the request entirely within the TTL window.

What you need to do on the Flutter side: The backend header provides defense-in-depth, but the real fix is making all 19 files use cachedLogbookSkillsProvider (which already exists in logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart) instead of calling repository.getLogbookSkills() directly.

API docs reference: See docs/logbook.md for the endpoint details.

docs.title: L2: getUpgradeEligibility() Fetched Redundantly
docs.text:
Status: No backend change

The upgrade eligibility endpoint serves user-specific data that varies by member, so a Cache-Control: public header is not appropriate. The fix is frontend-only: create a cachedUpgradeEligibilityProvider similar to your existing cachedLogbookSkillsProvider, with a 5-minute TTL via ApiCacheService.

API docs reference: See docs/upgrade-requests.md — Upgrade Eligibility section.

docs.title: L3: Trip Skill Opportunities = 2 API Calls Per Trip Detail View
docs.text:
Status: No backend change

Both getUpgradeEligibility() and getLogbookSkills() return user-level data that doesn't change between trip views. Cache them on the frontend side as recommended in L1 and L2.

docs.title: L4: Timeline Provider — N+1 Trip Detail Fetches
docs.text:
Status: No batch endpoint implemented

The enriched GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory endpoint (see below) now returns meetingPoint, image, and other fields that were previously missing. If the timeline provider was fetching individual trip details to get these fields, it can now use the trip history endpoint instead.

API docs reference: See docs/members.md — Member Trip History section for the full response field list.

docs.title: L5: Logbook Progress = 3 Cached API Calls
docs.text:
Status: No backend change needed

Your implementation is already well-done — 3 parallel calls with 5-minute TTL caching. The benefit of a composite endpoint is marginal here.

docs.title: C1: No HTTP-Level Caching (ETags/Last-Modified) — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED
docs.text:
Status: Cache-Control headers added to static endpoints

We added Cache-Control headers to endpoints that serve rarely-changing data:

Endpoint Cache-Control TTL GET /api/logbookskills/ public, max-age=600 10 min GET /api/levels/ public, max-age=1800 30 min GET /api/meetingpoints/ public, max-age=600 10 min GET /api/sponsors/ public, max-age=1800 30 min GET /api/faqs/ public, max-age=1800 30 min GET /api/choices/carbrand public, max-age=3600 60 min

ETag/Last-Modified support is deferred for now. Cache-Control provides the majority of the benefit with minimal implementation cost.

What you need to do on the Flutter side: Ensure your Dio client respects Cache-Control headers. If you use dio_cache_interceptor or similar, it should handle this automatically.

docs.title: C2: Notifications Fetched Without Pagination
docs.text:
Status: No backend change

The notifications endpoint currently returns the last 20 notifications (hard-coded limit). For the home badge, you can count isRead: false items from this set. A dedicated count endpoint is not needed at this stage.

API docs reference: See docs/notifications.md for endpoint details.

docs.title: C3: Admin Wizard Fetches ALL Trips (pageSize: 200 in a loop)
docs.text:
Status: Backend already supports server-side filtering

The GET /api/trips/ endpoint already supports all the filters the admin wizard needs: level__id, meetingPoint_Area, startTimeAfter, startTimeBefore, lead, approvalStatus. The frontend wizard should send these as query parameters instead of fetching all trips and filtering client-side.

Additionally, the new registered=true and waitlisted=true filters are now available.

API docs reference: See docs/trips.md — the Query Parameters table for the full list of supported filters.

docs.text: Status: No backend change needed (frontend-only fix as you noted)

docs.text: Status: No backend change needed (frontend-only fix as you noted)

docs.title: API Performance Audit Report
docs.text: Date: 2026-03-31 Scope: Full Flutter app — all API calls, caching, and data flow patterns Focus: Realistic backend changes to reduce API calls and improve performance

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
After auditing all 331 Dart files across 16 features, I identified 12 high-impact findings that can significantly reduce API calls. The app already has a solid ApiCacheService (TTL-based, stale-while-revalidate), but many screens and providers bypass it entirely or duplicate calls that could be consolidated.

The biggest wins come from: 1. Deduplicating the getLogbookSkills() catalog call — fetched independently by 19 files, often multiple times per session 2. Adding a backend composite/aggregate endpoint for Member Details (currently 6 parallel API calls) 3. Backend-side trip filtering to eliminate client-side re-filtering

docs.title: Finding T1: Trips List + Home Screen = Duplicate Trip Fetches
docs.text:
Files: trips_provider.dart, upcoming_trips_provider.dart Impact: 2 independent API calls for the same data on app launch

The home screen fetches upcoming trips via upcomingTripsProvider (pageSize: 100), and the trips list screen independently fetches via tripsProvider.loadTrips() (pageSize: 50). Both call GET /api/trips/ with nearly identical filters (approved, endTime > now).

Recommendation (Backend): No backend change needed — this is already partially addressed by the shared upcomingTripsProvider. However, the tripsProvider in the trips list screen does NOT reuse this cache. Consider having the trips list screen consume the same cached provider and apply local filters, or add a backend ETag/Last-Modified header so the Dio client can skip re-downloading identical data.

Recommendation (Quick backend win): Add Cache-Control: max-age=120 and ETag headers to GET /api/trips/. Dio can then send If-None-Match and get 304 Not Modified responses (~50 bytes) instead of the full JSON payload. This saves bandwidth even when data hasn't changed.

docs.title: Finding T2: Trip Detail Re-fetched on Every Navigation
docs.text:
File: trips_list_screen.dart:459 Impact: 1 API call every time user taps a trip card

ref.invalidate(tripDetailProvider(trip.id));
context.push('/trips/${trip.id}');

The code explicitly invalidates the cached trip detail before navigating. This means every tap = fresh API call, even if the user just viewed that trip 10 seconds ago.

Recommendation (Backend): Add ETag support to GET /api/trips/{id}/. The app can then always send the request but get a 304 response when nothing changed. This gives freshness guarantees without the full payload cost.

Alternative (Frontend-only): Remove the invalidate() call and let the autoDispose + staleness check handle it. The trip detail provider already uses FutureProvider.autoDispose, so navigating away disposes it and navigating back fetches fresh.

docs.title: Finding T3: Trip Actions Trigger Full List Refresh
docs.text:
File: trips_provider.dart:557-560 Impact: After register/unregister/waitlist, the entire trips list is refetched

await _ref.read(tripsProvider.notifier).refresh(); // re-fetches ALL trips

Every registration action calls refresh() which calls loadTrips() which fetches the full trips list again. This is heavy — up to 50 trips re-downloaded just because the user registered for one.

Recommendation (Backend): Return the updated trip object in the registration/unregistration response body. Currently the POST /api/trips/{id}/register likely returns a simple success message. If it returned the updated trip (with new registeredCount, isRegistered, isFull, etc.), the frontend could update just that one trip in the list without re-fetching everything.

Example response change:

// Current: {"message": "Successfully registered"}
// Proposed: {"message": "Successfully registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

docs.title: Finding T4: Member Details Screen — 6+ Waterfall API Calls
docs.text:
File: member_details_screen.dart:56-82 Impact: 6 independent API calls PER member view, some with waterfalls

_loadMemberData();           // 1. getMemberDetail()
_loadTripHistory(memberId);  // 2. getMemberTripHistory()
_loadTripStatistics(memberId); // 3. getMemberTripCounts() + 4. getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:1) + 5. getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:200) + 6. getMemberTripHistory(checkedIn:false)
_loadUpgradeHistory(memberId); // 7. getMemberUpgradeRequests()
_loadTripRequests(memberId);   // 8. getMemberTripRequests()
_loadMemberFeedback(memberId); // 9. getMemberFeedback()

The statistics section alone does 4 sequential calls: getMemberTripCounts(), then getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:1) for total count, then getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:200) for per-level breakdown, then another getMemberTripHistory(checkedIn:false) for upcoming count.

Recommendation (Backend — HIGH PRIORITY): Create a single composite endpoint: GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ that returns:

{
  "profile": { ...member data... },
  "tripCounts": { "total": 45, "checkedIn": 40, "asLeader": 12, "upcoming": 3 },
  "leaderByLevel": { "1": 5, "2": 4, "3": 3 },
  "recentTrips": [ ...last 10 trips... ],
  "upgradeRequests": [ ...list... ],
  "tripRequests": [ ...list... ],
  "feedback": [ ...list... ]
}

This reduces 9 API calls down to 1. This is a standard pattern (Google calls them "batch endpoints", Facebook uses "Graph API field expansion").

docs.title: Finding L1: getLogbookSkills() Called by 19 Files Independently (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
Impact: The skills catalog (GET /api/logbookskills/) is fetched independently by 19 different files. Each file calls repository.getLogbookSkills(pageSize: 100-500) directly without going through the cache.

Files making independent calls (bypassing cache): - trip_logbook_section_v2.dart — on every trip detail view - sign_off_bottom_sheet.dart — on every sign-off - bulk_sign_off_bottom_sheet.dart — on every bulk sign-off - trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart — on every trip detail view - member_logbook_screen.dart — on every logbook view - logbook_entry_detail_screen.dart — on every entry detail - timeline_provider.dart — on every timeline view - trip_skill_planning_provider.dart — on every planning view - certificate_provider.dart — on every certificate view - level_certificates_provider.dart — on every level cert view - migration_request_provider.dart — on every migration view - admin_sign_off_skills_screen.dart — on every admin sign-off - admin_create_logbook_entry_screen.dart — on every admin entry creation - logbook_provider.dart (admin) — on every admin logbook view - admin_logbook_data_provider.dart — on every admin data view - logbook_enrichment_service.dart — on enrichment - level_configuration_service.dart — on level config

Only 1 file uses the cache properly: logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart (via cachedLogbookSkillsProvider)

Recommendation (Backend — EASY WIN): Add Cache-Control: public, max-age=600 (10 minutes) to GET /api/logbookskills/. The skills catalog changes only when an admin modifies skill definitions — this is extremely rare. A 10-minute cache-control header would let the HTTP client skip the request entirely.

Recommendation (Frontend): Make all 19 files use cachedLogbookSkillsProvider instead of calling repository.getLogbookSkills() directly. This is a pure frontend fix but the backend cache header provides defense-in-depth.

docs.title: Finding L2: getUpgradeEligibility() Fetched Redundantly
docs.text:
Files: upgrade_progress_provider.dart, trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart, skills_matrix_v2_screen.dart, certificate_provider.dart, upgrade_certificate_provider.dart, trip_skill_planning_provider_v2.dart, create_upgrade_request_screen.dart Impact: 7 files call this endpoint independently, and the trip skill opportunities provider calls it ON EVERY TRIP DETAIL VIEW

The upgrade eligibility data (GET /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility) changes only when a logbook entry is signed off. Yet it's fetched: - When viewing logbook home - When viewing any trip detail (skill opportunities) - When viewing skills matrix - When viewing certificates - When creating upgrade request

Recommendation (Backend): Add Cache-Control: max-age=300 (5 minutes) to this endpoint. The data only changes after a logbook sign-off action, not on every page view.

Recommendation (Frontend): Create a cachedUpgradeEligibilityProvider similar to cachedLogbookSkillsProvider, using ApiCacheService with CacheCategory.logbookProgress and a 5-minute TTL. All 7 consumers would read from this single provider.

docs.title: Finding L3: Trip Skill Opportunities = 2 API Calls Per Trip Detail View
docs.text:
File: trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart:76-115 Impact: Every trip detail view triggers getUpgradeEligibility() + getLogbookSkills()

final eligibilityResponse = await repository.getUpgradeEligibility(user.id);
final skillsResponse = await repository.getLogbookSkills(pageSize: 200);

Both are user-level data that doesn't change between trip views.

Recommendation (Backend): Merge skill opportunities into the trip detail response. Add an optional ?expand=skillOpportunities parameter to GET /api/trips/{id}/. When present, the backend includes a skillOpportunities field with the user's relevant unmet requirements for that trip's level. This eliminates 2 extra API calls per trip view.

docs.title: Finding L4: Timeline Provider — N+1 Trip Detail Fetches
docs.text:
File: timeline_provider.dart:137-157 Impact: Fetches each trip individually via getTripDetail(id) in parallel — up to 15+ calls

final tripFutures = tripIds.map((id) async {
  final tripResponse = await repository.getTripDetail(id);
  return MapEntry(id, TripBasicInfo.fromJson(tripResponse));
});

While it uses Future.wait (good), it's still N separate HTTP requests. For a user with 15 trips in their timeline, that's 15 concurrent API calls.

Recommendation (Backend): Add a batch trip endpoint: GET /api/trips/batch/?ids=1,2,3,4,5 that returns multiple trips in one response. This is standard practice (Stripe, Slack, and GitHub all offer batch/bulk endpoints).

Alternative: Add expand=trip to GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries so the backend returns the trip object inline instead of just the trip ID. This eliminates the N+1 entirely.

docs.title: Finding L5: Logbook Progress = 3 Cached API Calls, But Still 3 Separate Calls
docs.text:
File: logbook_progress_provider.dart:36-52 Impact: 3 parallel API calls (cached with 5-min TTL) every time logbook home is visited

final results = await Future.wait([
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberLogbookSkills...),
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberLogbookEntries...),
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberTripCounts...),
]);

Credit: This is well-implemented with caching. But 3 separate HTTP calls could still be 1.

Recommendation (Backend): Create GET /api/members/{id}/logbook-summary/ returning:

{
  "skills": { "results": [...], "count": 45 },
  "entries": { "results": [...], "count": 20 },
  "tripCounts": { "total": 30, "checkedIn": 25 }
}

This collapses 3 calls into 1. With the existing 5-minute cache, this would mean 1 call every 5 minutes instead of 3.

docs.title: Finding C1: No HTTP-Level Caching (ETags/Last-Modified)
docs.text:
File: api_client.dart Impact: Every API call transfers the full response body, even when data hasn't changed

The Dio client has no If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since interceptor. The app-level cache (ApiCacheService) helps, but when TTLs expire, the full payload is always re-downloaded.

Recommendation (Backend): Add ETag and Last-Modified headers to all GET endpoints. Django REST Framework supports this via ConditionalGetMixin or middleware. This is a one-time backend change that benefits every endpoint:

# Django middleware or mixin
from django.utils.cache import patch_cache_control
from django.views.decorators.http import condition

# On DRF ViewSet:
class TripViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    @method_decorator(condition(last_modified_func=get_trips_last_modified))
    def list(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        ...

For the Flutter side, Dio supports 304 responses natively — no code change needed.

docs.title: Finding C2: Notifications Fetched Without Pagination
docs.text:
File: notification_provider.dart:51 Impact: Fetches ALL notifications every time, no pagination or limit

final response = await repository.getNotifications();

No pageSize, no limit. For active users with hundreds of notifications, this transfers a large payload.

Recommendation (Backend): 1. Add pageSize=50 default to the notifications endpoint 2. Add unread_only=true filter — the home badge only needs unread count, not all notification bodies 3. Better yet: Add a lightweight GET /api/notifications/count/ endpoint that returns just {"unread": 5} for the badge. The full list is only needed when the user opens the notifications screen.

docs.title: Finding C3: Admin Wizard Fetches ALL Trips (pageSize: 200 in a loop)
docs.text:
File: admin_wizard_provider.dart:62-67 Impact: Fetches ALL trips in the database, 200 at a time, in a while loop

const int pageSize = 200;
while (hasMorePages) {
  final response = await repository.getTrips(page: currentPage, pageSize: pageSize);
  ...
}

For a club with hundreds of trips, this downloads everything to the client for client-side filtering.

Recommendation (Backend): Move the admin wizard filtering entirely to the backend. The GET /api/trips/ endpoint already supports most of the filters (level_Id, meetingPoint_Area, startTimeAfter/Before, lead, ordering). The wizard should just send the final filter criteria as query params and let the backend return a single page of results. No pagination loop needed.

docs.title: Finding C4: getLogbookSkillReferences() Not Using Shared Cache
docs.text:
File: skills_comparison_provider.dart:39-58 Impact: Skills comparison fetches skill references for 2 members independently, bypassing cache

The cachedMemberSkillReferencesProvider exists in logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart but the comparison provider doesn't use it — it calls repository.getLogbookSkillReferences() directly.

Recommendation (Backend): No backend change needed. Recommendation (Frontend): Use cachedMemberSkillReferencesProvider in the comparison provider.

docs.title: Finding C5: Member Details Creates New Repository Instance
docs.text:
File: member_details_screen.dart:28 Impact: Bypasses the Riverpod-managed repository and cache

final _repository = MainApiRepository(); // creates new instance

This creates a fresh MainApiRepository (and therefore a fresh ApiClient with a fresh Dio instance) instead of using the Riverpod mainApiRepositoryProvider. This means: - No connection pooling with other screens - No shared interceptors state - No shared cache

Recommendation (Backend): No change needed. Recommendation (Frontend): Use ref.read(mainApiRepositoryProvider) instead.

docs.title: SECTION 4: PRIORITY RANKING
docs.text: Priority Finding API Calls Saved Backend Effort 1 L1: Cache-Control on /api/logbookskills/ ~15-20/session Add 1 header 2 T3: Return updated trip in register/unregister response ~3-5/session Modify response serializer 3 T4: GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ composite endpoint 8 calls -> 1 New endpoint, reuses existing querysets 4 L2: Cache-Control on /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility ~5-7/session Add 1 header 5 C1: ETag/Last-Modified on all GET endpoints 30-50% bandwidth Django middleware (one-time) 6 L3: ?expand=skillOpportunities on trip detail 2 calls/trip view New serializer field 7 C2: Notification count endpoint 1 call/screen view New lightweight endpoint 8 L5: GET /api/members/{id}/logbook-summary/ 3 -> 1 New composite endpoint 9 T2: ETag on trip detail 1 call/trip tap Part of C1 10 L4: expand=trip on logbook entries N calls -> 0 DRF expand support 11 C3: Backend-side admin wizard filtering Eliminates loop Already mostly supported 12 T1: Share trip cache between home and list 1 call/launch Frontend only

docs.title: SECTION 5: ESTIMATED IMPACT
docs.text:
Current state (typical user session): - App launch: ~8-10 API calls (home screen widgets + trips + notifications) - View trip details: ~4 API calls (trip detail + logbook skills + upgrade eligibility + skill opportunities) - View logbook: ~4 API calls (progress stats + skills catalog + entries + trip counts) - View member profile: ~9 API calls (profile + trips + stats + leader history x2 + upgrades + requests + feedback) - Total for a 15-minute browsing session: ~40-60 API calls

After implementing Priority 1-6: - App launch: ~5-6 API calls (deduplicated, cached) - View trip details: ~1-2 API calls (composite response, cached skills) - View logbook: ~1-2 API calls (composite endpoint, cached) - View member profile: ~1-2 API calls (summary endpoint) - Total for a 15-minute browsing session: ~12-20 API calls

Estimated reduction: 50-70% fewer API calls

docs.title: SECTION 6: WHAT BIG TECH WOULD DO
docs.text:
1. GraphQL or field expansion (Facebook/Meta): Instead of 9 REST calls for member details, one query that specifies exactly which fields/relations to include. Django Graphene or DRF's ?expand= pattern.

  2. ETag + Conditional GET (Google): Every GET response includes an ETag. Subsequent requests include If-None-Match, getting 304 Not Modified (zero body) when nothing changed. Django's ConditionalGetMiddleware does this automatically.

  3. Response includes mutation result (Stripe/Uber): After POST /register, the response includes the updated trip object. No need for a follow-up GET.

  4. Batch/composite endpoints (Google, Slack): GET /api/batch?endpoints=/trips/1,/trips/2,/trips/3 or purpose-built summary endpoints that join related data server-side.

  5. Cache-Control headers (Every CDN-aware service): Static-ish data (skill catalogs, level definitions, sponsors) gets Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600. Semi-static data gets max-age=300. The HTTP layer handles caching — no app code needed.

  6. Push-based invalidation (Firebase/Supabase): Instead of polling or TTL-based cache, the server pushes "trip 123 updated" events. The app already uses Firestore for chat — the same pattern could extend to trip state changes.

docs.text: Date: 2026-04-01 Scope: Address legitimate findings from Flutter and Website team audits Principle: Industry-standard patterns, zero breaking changes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After cross-referencing all three frontend audit documents against the actual backend code and current API documentation, we identified 6 actionable items. All documentation issues from the live test audit were already fixed in prior sessions. The items below are code changes only.

docs.title: Change 1: Add registered and waitlisted Filters to Trips Endpoint
docs.text: Priority: HIGH Source: BACKENDTODO #1, Performance Audit T3 File: api/filters.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add two custom filter methods to TripsFilter so that GET /api/trips/?registered=true returns only trips where the authenticated user is registered (and similarly for waitlisted=true).

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Add two BooleanFilter fields with custom method= handlers to TripsFilter. Each method will filter using Exists() subqueries against TripRegistration / TripWaitlist, referencing request.user. This is the standard django-filters pattern for request-aware filtering.

# In TripsFilter:
registered = filters.BooleanFilter(method='filter_registered')
waitlisted = filters.BooleanFilter(method='filter_waitlisted')

def filter_registered(self, queryset, name, value):
    user = self.request.user
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return queryset
    subquery = TripRegistration.objects.filter(trip=OuterRef('pk'), member=user)
    if value:
        return queryset.filter(Exists(subquery))
    return queryset.exclude(Exists(subquery))

def filter_waitlisted(self, queryset, name, value):
    # Same pattern with TripWaitlist

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. This is purely additive. Existing requests without the registered/waitlisted params behave identically.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Website team: Eliminates fetching all 3,305 trips and filtering client-side. Expected load time drop from 17-30s to <1s.
  • Flutter app: Can use same filter for "My Trips" screens.

docs.title: Change 2: Enrich Member Trip History Serializer
docs.text: Priority: HIGH Source: BACKENDTODO #1 (Option B) Files: api/serializers/serializers_trip.py, api/views/views_member.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add missing fields to MemberTripHistorySerializer so the website team doesn't need N+1 individual trip detail calls. Fields to add: image, meeting_point, registered_count, capacity, is_registered, is_waitlisted, allow_waitlist, approval_status.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Serializer changes — Extend MemberTripHistorySerializer to include the missing fields. Use the same patterns already established in ListTripSerializer:

class MemberTripHistorySerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    lead = ConciseMemberSerializer()
    level = LevelSerializer()
    meeting_point = MeetingPointSerializer()
    checked_in = serializers.BooleanField(source='member_checked_in')
    registered_count = serializers.IntegerField(read_only=True)
    is_registered = serializers.BooleanField(read_only=True)
    is_waitlisted = serializers.BooleanField(read_only=True)

    class Meta:
        model = Trip
        fields = (
            'id', 'title', 'description', 'start_time', 'end_time',
            'lead', 'level', 'checked_in', 'image', 'meeting_point',
            'registered_count', 'capacity', 'allow_waitlist',
            'approval_status', 'is_registered', 'is_waitlisted',
        )

View changes — Update the MemberTripHistory queryset to annotate registered_count, is_registered, and is_waitlisted using Count() and Exists() subqueries (same pattern already used in the view for member_checked_in). Also add select_related('meeting_point') which is already in the base mixin.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None (additive only). All existing fields remain. New fields are added to the response. The camelCase renderer will automatically convert registered_count -> registeredCount, is_registered -> isRegistered, etc.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Website team: Can use GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory as a drop-in replacement for fetching all trips. Response goes from 8 fields to 16 fields. Eliminates N+1 individual trip detail calls (each 3-13s).
  • Flutter app: Gets richer trip history data without extra calls.

docs.text: Priority: MEDIUM Source: Live Test Audit item 21.2 File: api/filters.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add date_joined as a DateFromToRangeFilter to MembersFilter, enabling GET /api/members/?date_joined_after=2026-03-01&date_joined_before=2026-04-01.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
class MembersFilter(filters.FilterSet):
    date_joined = DateFromToRangeFilter()

    class Meta:
        model = Member
        fields = {
            # ... existing fields ...
            'level__id': ['exact'],  # Also add this (Change 5)
        }

This follows the exact same pattern as start_time in TripsFilter and verdict_date in UpgradeRequestsFilter.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. Purely additive filter.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Admin users can filter members by join date (e.g., "new members this month").
  • Both frontend teams can use this for admin dashboard features.

docs.title: Change 4: Return Updated Trip in Registration Responses
docs.text: Priority: MEDIUM Source: Performance Audit T3 Files: api/views/views_trip.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: After a successful register/unregister/waitlist action, include the updated trip object in the response alongside the existing success message. This follows the Stripe/Uber pattern — mutations return the updated resource.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
After each successful registration action, serialize the trip using ListTripSerializer and include it in the response:

# In RegisterForTrip.post(), after successful registration:
trip.refresh_from_db()
trip_data = ListTripSerializer(trip, context={'request': request}).data
return Response({
    'success': True, 
    'message': msg,
    'trip': trip_data
}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)

Apply the same pattern to CancelTripRegistration and RegisterForTripWaitlist.

Queryset optimization: Before serializing, ensure the trip has proper prefetches:

trip = Trip.objects.select_related('lead', 'level', 'meeting_point') \
    .prefetch_related('tripregistration_set__member', 'tripwaitlist_set__member') \
    .annotate(
        registered_count=Count('tripregistration'),
        waitlist_count=Count('tripwaitlist')
    ).get(pk=trip.pk)

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. The existing success and message fields are preserved. The new trip field is additive. Frontends that don't read trip are unaffected.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Eliminates 3-5 follow-up GET calls per session after registration actions.
  • Both frontend teams get immediate UI updates without a second round-trip.

docs.title: Change 5: Add level__id Filter to Members
docs.text: Priority: LOW Source: Live Test Audit item 21.1 File: api/filters.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add level__id to MembersFilter.Meta.fields so admins can filter members by level ID.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
# In MembersFilter.Meta.fields, add:
'level__id': ['exact'],

One line. The level__numeric_level and level__name filters already work, but level__id is the most natural way to filter when you have a level dropdown that returns IDs.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. Additive filter.

docs.title: Change 6: Add Cache-Control Headers to Static-ish Endpoints
docs.text: Priority: LOW Source: Performance Audit L1, L2, C1 Files: api/views/ (multiple view files)

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add Cache-Control headers to endpoints that serve rarely-changing data, using Django's built-in @cache_control decorator. This is the standard HTTP caching pattern used by every CDN-aware service.

docs.title: Endpoints and TTLs
docs.text: Endpoint TTL Rationale GET /api/logbookskills/ 10 min (600s) Skills catalog changes only when admin edits definitions GET /api/levels/ 30 min (1800s) Levels almost never change GET /api/meetingpoints/ 10 min (600s) Meeting points rarely change GET /api/sponsors/ 30 min (1800s) Sponsor list changes rarely GET /api/faqs/ 30 min (1800s) FAQ content changes rarely GET /api/choices/carbrand 60 min (3600s) Car brand list is essentially static

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Use Django's @method_decorator(cache_control(...)) on the list action of each ViewSet:

from django.utils.decorators import method_decorator
from django.views.decorators.cache import cache_control

class LogbookSkillViewSet(viewsets.ReadOnlyModelViewSet):
    @method_decorator(cache_control(public=True, max_age=600))
    def list(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        return super().list(request, *args, **kwargs)

For endpoints that include user-specific data (trips, members), we do NOT add caching headers — those must remain private / no-cache by default.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. Cache-Control headers are advisory. Clients that don't implement HTTP caching are unaffected. Clients with Dio/OkHttp/Axios will automatically benefit.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Reduces redundant fetches of static data (logbook skills fetched by 19 Flutter files independently).
  • Saves bandwidth on every cache hit (304 Not Modified or skip entirely).

The individual endpoints are fast enough when cached properly. Batch trip endpoint GET /api/trips/batch/?ids=1,2,3 Not implementing N+1 is a frontend issue (timeline provider). Frontend should use shared cache provider. GET /api/members/{id}/logbook-summary/ Not implementing Same as above — composite endpoints add maintenance burden. ?expand=skillOpportunities on trip detail Not implementing GraphQL-style field expansion is over-engineering for this project size. ETag/Last-Modified on all endpoints Not implementing now Cache-Control headers (Change 6) provide 80% of the benefit with 10% of the effort. ETags require per-endpoint last_modified_func implementations. Can revisit later. Notifications count endpoint Not implementing Current hard-coded limit of 20 is reasonable. Frontend can count isRead: false from that set. Trailing slash standardization Not implementing Already documented. Django's URL routing makes this non-trivial to change without breaking existing clients.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
We reviewed both requests from the website team. Request #1 (server-side filtering for user's trips) has been fully addressed with two backend changes. Request #2 (trailing-slash inconsistency) is acknowledged but will not be changed.

No breaking changes. All changes are additive.

docs.title: Request #1: Server-side filtering for user's registered/waitlisted trips — IMPLEMENTED
docs.text: We implemented both of your recommended options:

docs.title: Option A: registered and waitlisted filters on GET /api/trips/
docs.text:
The trips list endpoint now supports two new query parameters:

GET /api/trips/?registered=true          -> only trips where the authenticated user is registered
GET /api/trips/?registered=false         -> only trips where the authenticated user is NOT registered
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true          -> only trips where the authenticated user is on the waitlist
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=false         -> only trips where the authenticated user is NOT on the waitlist

These filters can be combined with all existing filters:

# User's past registered trips (approved only)
GET /api/trips/?registered=true&approvalStatus=A&startTimeBefore=2026-04-01

# User's upcoming registered trips
GET /api/trips/?registered=true&approvalStatus=A&startTimeAfter=2026-04-01

# User's waitlisted trips
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true&approvalStatus=A

Implementation details: - Uses efficient Exists() subqueries — no client-side filtering needed - Requires authentication (anonymous requests ignore the filter) - Returns the full trip object with all fields (isRegistered, isWaitlisted, registeredCount, capacity, meetingPoint, image, etc.)

Expected impact on your "My Trips" portal page: - Past tab: Response drops from 3,305 trips (95 KB) to just the user's trips (~15-20 trips, ~15 KB) - Load time should drop from 17-30 seconds to under 1 second

docs.title: Option B: Enriched GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory
docs.text:
The trip history endpoint now returns all the fields your portal needs. Previously it returned 8 fields; it now returns 17:

New fields added: | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | image | string/null | Trip cover photo URL | | meetingPoint | object/null | {id, name, area, lat, lon, link} | | registeredCount | integer | Number of registered members | | capacity | integer | Trip capacity | | isRegistered | boolean | Whether the target member is registered | | isWaitlisted | boolean | Whether the target member is on the waitlist | | allowWaitlist | boolean | Whether the trip allows waitlisting | | approvalStatus | string | Approval status (A, P, C) |

Previously existing fields (unchanged): id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead, level, checkedIn

docs.title: Which option should you use?
docs.text:
For the "My Trips" portal page, we recommend Option A (GET /api/trips/?registered=true): - Returns the full trip list schema with all fields you need - Supports pagination, date range filters, and ordering - Cleanly separates "upcoming" vs "past" with startTimeAfter/startTimeBefore - One endpoint handles both registered and waitlisted trips

Option B (triphistory) is better for viewing another member's trip history (admin use case), since the registered filter on /api/trips/ only works for the authenticated user's own trips.

docs.title: Example: Building the My Trips portal
docs.text:
# Upcoming tab (registered)
GET /api/trips/?registered=true&approvalStatus=A&startTimeAfter=2026-04-01&pageSize=50

# Upcoming tab (waitlisted)
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true&approvalStatus=A&startTimeAfter=2026-04-01&pageSize=50

# Past tab
GET /api/trips/?registered=true&approvalStatus=A&startTimeBefore=2026-04-01&ordering=-startTime&pageSize=50

API docs reference: See docs/trips.md — the Query Parameters table documents all available filters including the new registered and waitlisted parameters.

docs.title: Request #2: Trailing-slash inconsistency — NOT CHANGING
docs.text:
We acknowledge the inconsistency. The pattern is:

  • Main resource endpoints (router-registered ViewSets): require trailing slash (/api/trips/, /api/members/)
  • Sub-action endpoints (manually wired paths): require NO trailing slash (/api/trips/search, /api/members/{id}/triphistory)
  • Choices endpoints: require NO trailing slash (/api/choices/carbrand)

This is a consequence of Django REST Framework's DefaultRouter (which adds trailing slashes) vs manual path() definitions (which don't). Changing this would risk breaking existing clients (Flutter app, website) that already handle the current pattern.

The pattern is fully documented in our API docs. Each endpoint's documentation specifies whether it uses a trailing slash or not. When in doubt, check the relevant doc page:

Document Endpoints covered docs/trips.md All trip endpoints including registration, approval, search docs/members.md All member endpoints including triphistory, tripcounts, search docs/trip-search.md Trip search endpoint docs/vehicles.md Vehicle CRUD + car brand choices docs/notifications.md Notifications + notification settings docs/api-concepts.md General API patterns including trailing slash reference

docs.title: Backend API Documentation Audit
docs.text:
Purpose: This report documents every discrepancy found between the backend API documentation (ad4x4-backend/docs/) and the actual live API behaviour. Each item tells the backend team exactly what to fix in their docs.

Tested by: Frontend AI developer (Session #14) Date: 2026-03-30 API base: https://ap.ad4x4.com Test user: hani amj (ID 10613, Board member, admin permissions) Method: Every endpoint was tested with curl + Bearer JWT token

Scope limitation: All tests were performed with a Board member (admin) account that has full permissions. This means: - Covered: Endpoint URLs, trailing slashes, HTTP methods, response field names/structures, filter parameters, pagination, query validation — all verified. - NOT covered: Permission-gated behaviour. Endpoints that restrict access or hide fields based on user level were not tested with a lower-permission account. Examples: - GET /api/members/ may hide phone/email fields for users without VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission. - GET /api/members/search requires SEARCH_MEMBERS permission — a Newbie may get 403. - GET /api/upgraderequests/ requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission. - Trip registration vehicle_required enforcement may differ for staff vs regular users. - Self-only restrictions (e.g., editing own profile vs another member's) not tested. - Recommendation: When building features that use permission-restricted endpoints, test with a regular member account (e.g., Newbie or Intermediate level) to verify the actual permission behaviour.

docs.text:
During the audit, we discovered an undocumented field lastUserActivity in the notification settings response:

GET /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings
→ {
    "clubNewsEnabledEmail": true,

    "newTripAlertsEnabledEmail": true,

docs.text: Project: AD4x4 Django REST API Audit Date: 2026-03-24 Auditor: Automated + Manual Code Review Scope: Full codebase, dependencies, configuration, infrastructure Codebase Size: 13,177 lines of Python across 80+ files Django Version: 5.1 | DRF: 3.17.1 | Python: 3.13

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
This audit identified 42 security findings across the AD4x4 Django application:

Severity Count Description CRITICAL 6 Immediate exploitation risk, could lead to full system compromise HIGH 17 Significant vulnerabilities requiring urgent remediation MEDIUM 13 Notable weaknesses requiring planned remediation LOW 6 Minor issues and hardening recommendations

Top 3 Risks: 1. Firebase service account private key committed to Git - allows full Firebase project takeover 2. JWT tokens never expire - permanent authentication bypass if any token is leaked 3. Path traversal in media serving - arbitrary file read from server filesystem

docs.title: C1: Firebase Service Account Private Key Committed to Repository
docs.text:
Field Value Severity CRITICAL CVSS 9.8 CWE CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials) Location infra/app/config/ad4x4-5ce99.json OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

Evidence:

Type: service_account
Project ID: ad4x4-5ce99
Client Email: firebase-adminsdk-cjegh@ad4x4-5ce99.iam.gserviceaccount.com
Private Key ID: d4f776920783b6e45a11da2696d7badeb5893225
Has Private Key: True (full RSA private key, 1704 bytes)

The complete Firebase Admin SDK service account JSON file, including the full RSA private key, is committed to the Git repository (commit 2f188d3 - "Add FCM config to git"). Anyone with repository access can: - Send push notifications to any user - Create custom Firebase auth tokens for any user - Access any Firebase service the service account has permissions for - Impersonate the backend server

Remediation: 1. IMMEDIATELY rotate the Firebase service account key in the Google Cloud Console 2. Remove the file from Git history using git filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner 3. Add *.json service account patterns to .gitignore 4. Store credentials in a secrets manager (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.)

docs.title: C2: JWT Tokens Have No Expiration (Permanent Authentication Tokens)
C3: Path Traversal Vulnerability in Media File Serving
docs.text:
Field Value Severity CRITICAL CVSS 8.6 CWE CWE-22 (Path Traversal) Location api/views/views_media.py:10-15 OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

Evidence (api/views/views_media.py):

@api_view(['GET'])
def serve_media(request, path):
    full_path = os.path.join(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, path)
    if os.path.exists(full_path) and os.path.isfile(full_path):
        response = FileResponse(open(full_path, 'rb'), content_type='application/octet-stream')
        response['Access-Control-Allow-Origin'] = '*'
        return response

Proof of Concept (tested in sandbox):

Input: ../../../etc/passwd
  os.path.join result: /app/uploads/../../../etc/passwd
  Normalized: /etc/passwd
  Stays within MEDIA_ROOT: False  <-- ESCAPES!

Input: avatars/../../../etc/passwd
  os.path.join result: /app/uploads/avatars/../../../etc/passwd
  Normalized: /etc/passwd
  Stays within MEDIA_ROOT: False  <-- ESCAPES!

The path parameter from the URL uploads/<path:path> is passed directly to os.path.join() without any validation that the resulting path stays within MEDIA_ROOT. Django's <path:path> URL converter accepts ../ sequences.

Impact: An attacker can read any file on the server that the application user has read access to, including: - /app/config/*.json (Firebase service account keys) - /etc/passwd (system user enumeration) - Application source code - Environment variables from /proc/self/environ

Remediation:

import os
from django.http import FileResponse, HttpResponseNotFound, HttpResponseForbidden

@api_view(['GET'])
def serve_media(request, path):
    full_path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, path))
    media_root = os.path.realpath(settings.MEDIA_ROOT)

    # Prevent path traversal
    if not full_path.startswith(media_root + os.sep):
        return HttpResponseForbidden('Access denied')

    if os.path.exists(full_path) and os.path.isfile(full_path):
        response = FileResponse(open(full_path, 'rb'))
        return response
    return HttpResponseNotFound('File not found')

Field Value Severity CRITICAL CVSS 8.1 CWE CWE-942 (Permissive Cross-domain Policy) Location ad4x4/settings.py:406 OWASP A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration

Evidence:

CORS_ORIGIN_ALLOW_ALL = True

This allows any website on the internet to make authenticated cross-origin requests to the API. Combined with SessionAuthentication being enabled, an attacker can create a malicious webpage that makes API requests using a victim's session cookies.
