docs.title: C5: Sensitive Data Logged in Plaintext (Passwords in Logs)
C6: Deactivated/Deleted Users Can Still Authenticate via JWT
docs.text:
Field Value Severity CRITICAL CVSS 8.8 CWE CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization) Location api/util.py:92-108 OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

Evidence (api/util.py lines 98-103):

user_class = get_user_model()
try:
    user = user_class.objects.get(pk=user_id)   # <-- No is_active check!
except user_class.DoesNotExist:
    msg = _('User not found.')
    raise AuthenticationFailed(msg) from None

The custom JWTAuthentication.authenticate() method retrieves the user by primary key but never checks user.is_active. Combined with: - The anonymize_data() method in models_member.py which sets is_active = False but does not invalidate tokens - The AccountDeletionRequest flow which deactivates accounts after 3 days - The fact that tokens never expire (C2)

This means a deactivated, suspended, or deleted user's existing JWT token continues to work indefinitely.

Impact: Users who have been banned, suspended, or who requested account deletion can continue accessing all API endpoints using their old tokens.

Remediation:

user = user_class.objects.get(pk=user_id)
if not user.is_active:
    msg = _('User account is disabled.')
    raise AuthenticationFailed(msg) from None

SECRET_KEY = 'dev-secret-key-123463sdf12349erwh2837h'

docs.title: H5: IDOR Vulnerabilities on 5 Member Endpoints
docs.text:
Location api/views/views_member.py CWE CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key) OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

The following endpoints accept an arbitrary member pk in the URL and return that member's data without verifying the requesting user is authorized to view it:

Endpoint Data Exposed GET /api/members/<pk>/triphistory Full trip history with registration dates GET /api/members/<pk>/triprequests All trip requests GET /api/members/<pk>/logbookentries Logbook entries with comments GET /api/members/<pk>/logbookskills Skill references and sign-offs GET /api/members/<pk>/tripcounts Detailed trip statistics per level

Any authenticated user can enumerate through member IDs (1, 2, 3, ...) and extract all other members' activity data.

Remediation: Add ownership check or limit to request.user.pk == pk (with admin override).

docs.title: H6: Mass Assignment Risk via exclude Pattern in Serializers
docs.text:
Location api/serializers/serializers_member.py CWE CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes)

Three serializers use exclude instead of explicit fields:

class EditMemberSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Member
        exclude = ('password','is_staff','is_superuser','is_active',
                   'date_joined','last_login')

The level, trip_count, paid_member, and title fields are not excluded, meaning: - level (ReadOnlyField) is safe due to serializer field override - trip_count — NOT protected, user could manipulate their trip count - paid_member — NOT protected, user could set themselves as paid - title — NOT protected

If any new sensitive field is added to the Member model in the future, it becomes automatically writable via the API.

Remediation: Switch all serializers from exclude to explicit fields lists.

docs.title: H7: No Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints (Django Level)
H8: Password Change Doesn't Invalidate Existing Tokens
docs.text:
Location api/views/views_auth.py:23-34 CWE CWE-613 
def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
    serializer = self.get_serializer(data=request.data)
    ...
    user.set_password(serializer.validated_data['password'])
    user.save()
    return Response({'success': True, 'message': 'password_changed'})

After a password change, all existing JWT tokens remain valid because: 1. The JWT payload only contains user_id (no password hash, no token version) 2. Tokens never expire (see C2) 3. Token revocation raises AuthTokenNotRevoked()

If an account is compromised and the password is changed, the attacker's stolen token still works forever.

Remediation: Implement a token version/generation counter on the User model. Increment on password change. Validate in JWTAuthentication.authenticate().

docs.title: H9: DEBUG Falls to True Without Environment Variable
docs.text:
Location ad4x4/settings.py:69-79 
DEBUG = False
if os.getenv('DJANGO_SECRET_KEY'):
    SECRET_KEY = os.getenv('DJANGO_SECRET_KEY')
    DEV = False
else:
    SECRET_KEY = 'dev-secret-key-...'
    DEV = True
    DEBUG = True  # <-- Enabled when env var missing

If DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is accidentally unset or the env file is not loaded, the application runs with DEBUG=True in production, exposing: - Full stack traces with source code - Django debug toolbar (if installed) - Database query logs - All settings values - Template variable dump

Remediation: DEBUG = os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'False').lower() == 'true' — Never default to True.

Location infra/.env.example:32 CWE CWE-798 
RESTIC_PASSWORD=ad4x4-r3st1c-Redbeard

If this is the real password, anyone with repo access can decrypt all Restic backups stored on Backblaze B2.

Remediation: Change the Restic password immediately. Replace with your-restic-password-here in .env.example.

docs.title: H11: Unauthenticated Member Profile Listing
docs.text:
Location api/views/views_member.py:124-125 CWE CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information) 
def get_permissions(self):
    if self.action in ['list', 'retrieve']:
        permission_classes = (drf_permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly,)

IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly allows unauthenticated GET requests. The ProfileSerializer exposes: - Username, email, full name - Phone number (via ContactInfoMemberSerializer) - Date of birth - Emergency contact name and phone - City, gender, nationality - Avatar URL - Member level and trip count

This is a PII disclosure to anyone who can access the API.

Remediation: Change to IsAuthenticated for list and retrieve. Consider a PublicMemberSerializer with minimal fields for unauthenticated access if needed.

H15: No File Type Validation on Upload Fields
docs.text:
Location Multiple models CWE CWE-434 (Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type)

The project has 11 ImageField/FileField upload points across models: - Member.avatar — Only validates size (2.5 MB), not type - UpgradeRequest.attachment — No upload_to path, no validation at all - LogbookMigrationPDF.uploaded_pdf — FileField accepts any file type - TripReport.track_file — FileField accepts any file type - ClubNews.image, Feedback.image, Sponsor.image, Vehicle.image, Trip.image, TripReportImage.image

While Django's ImageField uses Pillow to verify image headers, this can be bypassed with polyglot files (valid image + embedded script). The FileField instances have no content validation at all.

The avatar clean() method only checks size:

def clean(self):
    if self.avatar and self.avatar.size > 2.5 * 1024 * 1024:
        raise ValidationError("Avatar file size must be less than 2.5 MB.")

Remediation: Add file type validation using django-upload-validator or custom validators. Enforce allowed MIME types. Serve uploaded files from a separate domain.

docs.title: M13: Raw SQL in GeocodingCache.truncate() Without Parameterization
docs.text:
Location api/models/models_geocoding_cache.py:58-61 CWE CWE-89 (SQL Injection) 
@classmethod
def truncate(cls):
    table = cls._meta.db_table
    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute(f'TRUNCATE TABLE "{table}" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;')

While the table name comes from Django's model metadata (not user input) and is therefore not directly injectable, this use of raw SQL: - Bypasses Django's ORM safety net - Sets a risky pattern that developers may copy with user-supplied values - Is called from a signal (api/signals.py:170) that could be triggered unexpectedly

Remediation: Use cls.objects.all().delete() instead, or if TRUNCATE is needed for performance, add a comment explaining why raw SQL is safe here.

The AD4x4 Backend is a well-structured Django REST API with solid foundations in layered architecture, permission management, and service patterns. docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Build a companion website to the AD4x4 mobile app focused on payment processing to avoid Apple/Google app store commissions. The website shares the same Member database and authentication as the existing backend.

Target Users: Potential and existing members who want to pay for premium membership via the web to avoid in-app purchase fees.

docs.title: Existing Backend
docs.text:
• Member Model: api/models/models_member.py - extends AbstractUser
  • Payment Field: paid_member (BooleanField, default=False) - exists
  • Payment Endpoint: POST /api/members/<id>/payments - requires edit_membership_payments permission
  • Authentication: JWT via SimpleJWT + rest_registration library
  • Email: Already configured (Gmail SMTP)

docs.title: Rest_registration Already Provides
docs.text:
• /api/auth/login/ - Login
  • /api/auth/register/ - Registration
  • /api/auth/password/reset/ - Password reset (URL configured: https://web.ad4x4.com/reset-password)
  • /api/auth/password/reset/confirm/ - Password reset confirmation

docs.title: Settings Already in Place
docs.text:
• Django templates: Configured in TEMPLATES
  • Static files: Configured (STATIC_ROOT, STATICFILES_DIRS)
  • ALLOWED_HOSTS: Includes web.ad4x4.com (via existing config)

docs.title: 2. Requirements Summary
docs.text: Feature Description Signup Member registration via web form Login Existing member login Password Recovery Reset password flow App Store Links Links to download the mobile apps PayPal Payment One-time payment to set paid_member=True Payment Verification Server-side via PayPal IPN/webhook

docs.title: 1.1 Create Website App
docs.text:
• Create new Django app: python manage.py startapp website
  • Add 'website' to INSTALLED_APPS in settings.py
  • Create website/ directory structure with views.py, urls.py, templates/

docs.title: 1.2 URL Configuration
docs.text:
• Add website URLs to ad4x4/urls.py:
  • / - Home/Landing page
  • /signup/ - Registration page
  • /login/ - Login page
  • /logout/ - Logout page
  • /reset-password/ - Password reset (can use rest_registration template)
  • /reset-password/confirm/<reset_token>/ - Password reset confirm
  • /payment/ - Payment page
  • /payment/success/ - Payment success page
  • /payment/cancel/ - Payment cancel page
  • /payment/webhook/ - PayPal webhook endpoint

docs.title: 1.3 Static Files & Media
docs.text:
• Create static/website/ directory for CSS, JS, images
  • Create basic styling (or use existing CSS framework)
  • Add app store badge images (Apple App Store, Google Play)

docs.title: 2.1 Base Template
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/base.html
  • Include navbar with logo, login/logout links
  • Include footer with app store links
  • Add Bootstrap 5 CDN (or Tailwind)

docs.title: 2.2 Login View
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/login.html
  • Form: username/email, password, remember me
  • Link to password reset
  • Link to signup
  • Implement website/views.py:LoginView using Django's authenticate() + session login
  • Handle "next" parameter for redirect after login

docs.title: 2.3 Signup View
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/signup.html
  • Form: username, email, password, confirm password
  • Use existing MemberRegistrationSerializer logic
  • Implement website/views.py:SignupView
  • On success: auto-login and redirect to payment page

docs.title: 2.4 Password Reset Views
docs.text:
• Use rest_registration's built-in templates OR create custom
  • Create templates/website/password_reset.html - request reset
  • Create templates/website/password_reset_confirm.html - set new password
  • Configure rest_registration to use custom template paths

docs.title: 2.5 Logout View
docs.text:
• Implement website/views.py:LogoutView
  • Use Django's logout() function
  • Redirect to home page

docs.title: 3.1 PayPal Configuration
docs.text:
• Add to settings.py: python PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID = os.getenv('PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID') PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv('PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET') PAYPAL_MODE = 'live' # or 'sandbox' PAYPAL_PRODUCT_PRICE = '9.99' # one-time payment amount
  • Get PayPal client ID/secret from PayPal Developer Dashboard

docs.title: 3.2 PayPal JS SDK Integration
docs.text:
• Add PayPal SDK script to payment template
  • Create JavaScript to render PayPal buttons
  • Handle order creation and capture

docs.title: 3.3 Payment View
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/payment.html
  • Display pricing, features of paid membership
  • Show PayPal button
  • On successful payment:
  • Capture order via PayPal API
  • Set member.paid_member = True
  • Redirect to success page

docs.title: 3.4 Webhook Handler (Server-side Verification)
docs.text:
• Create website/views.py:PayPalWebhookView
  • Endpoint: POST /payment/webhook/
  • Verify webhook signature
  • Handle PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED event
  • Fallback: Also support client-side order capture for immediate feedback

docs.title: 3.5 Success/Cancel Pages
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/payment_success.html
  • Create templates/website/payment_cancel.html
  • Display appropriate messages

docs.title: 4.1 API Endpoint for Setting Paid Status
docs.text:
• Create new endpoint (or modify existing): POST /api/website/mark-paid/
  • Accept: memberid, paypalorderid, paypaltransaction_id
  • Verify transaction with PayPal API
  • Set member.paid_member = True
  • Log payment for audit trail
  • Protect with CSRF + authentication

docs.title: 4.2 Payment Model (Optional - for records)
docs.text:
• Create WebsitePayment model:
  • member (FK to Member)
  • amount
  • currency
  • paypalorderid
  • paypaltransactionid
  • status (pending, completed, failed)
  • createdat, updatedat

docs.title: 5.1 Home Page
docs.text:
• Create templates/website/home.html
  • Hero section with app description
  • App store download buttons (prominent)
  • "Upgrade to Premium" CTA (for logged-in non-paying members)
  • Features overview

docs.title: 5.2 Authenticated Home (for logged-in users)
docs.text:
• Show personalized content based on membership status
  • If not paid_member: show upgrade prompt
  • If paid_member: show "You're a premium member"

docs.title: 6.1 CSRF & Authentication
docs.text:
• Ensure all forms use {% csrf_token %}
  • Use @login_required decorator on views requiring auth
  • Configure session authentication (add to DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES)

docs.title: 6.2 Environment Variables
docs.text:
• Document required env vars:
  • PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID
  • PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET
  • PAYPAL_MODE (sandbox/live)

docs.title: 6.3 Docker & Infrastructure
docs.text: The website uses the same domain as the API (ap.ad4x4.com) - website at /, API at /api/.

docs.title: 6.3.1 Docker Configuration
docs.text:
• Add website app files to Dockerapp: dockerfile # Add website app COPY --chown=appuser:appuser ./website ./website COPY --chown=appuser:appuser ./static/website ./static/website

  • Pass PayPal env vars to ad4x4-app container in docker-compose

docs.title: 6.3.2 Nginx Configuration
docs.text:
No separate vhost needed - website served at /, API at /api/:

  • Existing nginx config already handles this pattern
  • Website URLs don't conflict with API routes

docs.title: Authentication Decision
docs.text: The website uses session authentication (different from the app's JWT): - Add rest_framework.authentication.SessionAuthentication to settings - Use Django's auth.login() / auth.logout() - The API endpoints for payment use JWT but website uses session

docs.title: Member Sync
docs.text:
• Website and app share same Member model
  • Member registers on website → appears in app
  • Member pays on website → paid_member=True → works in app

docs.title: PayPal Flow
docs.text:
1. User clicks PayPal button on payment page
  2. PayPal SDK shows checkout UI
  3. User approves payment
  4. JavaScript captures order, gets transaction ID
  5. JS sends transaction ID to Django endpoint
  6. Django verifies with PayPal API (server-side)
  7. Django sets member.paid_member = True
  8. Redirect to success page

docs.title: 8. Testing Checklist
docs.text:
• Signup flow works (new user created, can login)
  • Login flow works (existing user can login)
  • Password reset flow works (receive email, reset password)
  • PayPal payment flow works (sandbox mode)
  • Paid member status updates correctly in database
  • Logged-in non-paying users see upgrade prompt
  • Logged-in paying users see "premium member"
  • App store links open correct stores
